title: Quantity Surveyor Salary: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and Tax in 2026-27
description: Calculate a quantity surveyor salary from hourly rates to annual pay. Includes award rates, casual loading, tax brackets, and super guarantee for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a quantity surveyor earning $54.83 per hour (based on ABS average weekly earnings of $2,083.70 for full-time adults), the annual gross pay for a 38-hour week is approximately $108,400 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a quantity surveyor under the Surveying Award?
faqs.a: Under the Surveying Award 2020, quantity surveyors are typically classified at Level 4 or Level 5. As of 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rate for a Level 4 employee is $38.16, and for Level 5 it is $37.24. These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $47.70 for Level 4 and $46.55 for Level 5.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a quantity surveyor salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Surveying Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, a Level 4 casual quantity surveyor would be paid $47.70 per hour for ordinary hours (compared to $38.16 for a permanent employee). This loading is intended to compensate for entitlements like paid leave. When using our timesheet calculator, you can check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% to your base rate.

faqs.q: What is the typical annual salary for a quantity surveyor in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70. For a quantity surveyor working 38 hours per week, this equates to an hourly rate of about $54.83 and an annual gross salary of approximately $108,400. Actual salaries vary by experience, location, and employer. Many quantity surveyors are employed under enterprise agreements or individual contracts that may exceed award rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Quantity Surveyor Salary

If you are a quantity surveyor or considering a career in this field, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential. Whether you are negotiating a salary offer or checking your current pay, the formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. This article explains the key components of a **quantity surveyor salary**, including award rates, casual loading, tax, and superannuation.

## Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The Surveying Award 2020 (MA000066) sets minimum pay rates for employees in the surveying industry, including quantity surveyors. As of 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission increased award rates by 4.75%. The award classifies workers into 12 levels. Quantity surveyors are typically classified at Level 4 or Level 5, depending on qualifications and responsibilities. The minimum hourly rate for Level 4 is $38.16, and for Level 5 it is $37.24.

For comparison, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Most quantity surveyors earn well above this, but the award provides a safety net. If you are covered by an enterprise agreement, the rates in that agreement apply instead.

## Typical Quantity Surveyor Salary

While award rates set a floor, many quantity surveyors earn significantly more. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026. For a 38-hour week, that is an hourly rate of $54.83. Using the formula **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**, the annual gross pay would be about $108,400. This is a useful benchmark for a typical **quantity surveyor salary**, though actual pay depends on experience, location, and specialisation.

If you are paid a salary, you can convert it to an hourly rate by dividing by 52 and then by your weekly hours. For part-time employees, the award applies pro-rata based on 38 ordinary hours for full-time.

## Casual Loading and Fortnightly Pay

Casual employees under the Surveying Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, a Level 4 casual quantity surveyor would be paid $47.70 per hour (125% of $38.16). This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% to your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For a typical full-time quantity surveyor earning $2,083.70 per week, that would be $4,167.40 per fortnight.

## Tax and Superannuation

Tax is calculated using the 2026-27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $45,000, 37% to $135,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a quantity surveyor earning $108,400, the tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $24,867 plus Medicare $2,168, total $26,867. The actual amount may differ if you have HELP loans or salary packaging.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% of ordinary earnings, capped at $270,830 per year. For a $108,400 salary, that is $13,008 in super, paid into your fund. This is an estimate, not a determination.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion] helps you calculate annual, fortnightly, and monthly pay. You can also view [pay guides](/blog] for award rates and [reference tables](/data] for ABS earnings. For a quantity surveyor salary, use the base hourly rate and adjust for casual loading if applicable.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2027-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
